questions.q: What was Finance's original request from Lesson 1, that this report finally answers?
options: A one-time Athena query someone runs whenever they remember to
The same regional revenue numbers every month, without anyone hand-writing or re-running a query
A report that only Ops can access
A dashboard with no underlying SQL at all
questions.explain: Finance's actual ask in Lesson 1 was repeatability and trust, not just the ability to query the data at all.

questions.q: Which two dimension tables does the Finance report's query join to `analytics.fact_orders`?
options: dim_customer and dim_date
dim_product and dim_customer
dim_product and dim_date
No dimension tables; it reads only fact_orders
questions.explain: The query joins fact_orders to dim_product (for category) and dim_date (for year and month).

questions.q: Why does this report live in Redshift rather than Athena, even though Athena can already query the curated data (Lesson 7)?
options: Athena cannot read Parquet files
It's a genuine multi-table join run repeatedly with consistent performance expectations — exactly the workload a warehouse is built for
Redshift is required by AWS for any report with more than one column
Athena was decommissioned after Lesson 7
questions.explain: A recurring, multi-table join against a stable schema is the workload Redshift exists for; Athena remains better suited to lighter, ad hoc access.

questions.q: Where does the `order_total` column used in this report's SUM come from?
options: It's typed manually into the Redshift Query Editor each month
A computed column added by the Glue ETL job back in Lesson 3
It's generated randomly by Redshift at query time
It comes from the raw, uncleaned S3 zone
questions.explain: order_total was one of the three fixes the northfield-orders-etl Glue job applied during the ETL build in Lesson 3.

questions.q: What makes this query a 'recurring report' rather than an ad hoc one?
options: It is saved and re-run against freshly loaded data after each refresh, instead of being retyped from scratch every time
It uses the word SELECT instead of a stored procedure
It only runs once and is then deleted
It requires a brand-new Redshift workgroup every month
questions.explain: The defining trait of a recurring report is reusing the same saved logic against new data, not reproducing the logic by hand each time.
